source.title: Precise Dynamics of Diagonal Linear Networks: A Unifying Analysis by Dynamical Mean-Field Theory

record.tranche_reason: Analyzes how initialization scale relates to generalization and convergence in diagonal linear networks, using a different model and analysis from the claim versions. It does not test the specific behaviors named in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper reports initialization-dependent fixed-point test error, convergence rates, and an explicit relation between susceptibility and the training/test error ratio. Its numerical values for the initialization sweeps are shown in figures; the text supplies qualitative descriptions. Cited prior-work results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study cites Neyshabur et al. (2015) as background on implicit bias, but its own results test none of V1–V8. It studies initialization-dependent sparse regression and convergence in diagonal linear networks. Its sample-to-feature ratio analysis is not a network-width sweep, and susceptibility is not magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for unregularized, overparameterized sparse regression: smaller initialization improves fixed-point generalization while slowing convergence. The authors leave extension of this trade-off to general neural networks as future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes two-layer diagonal linear networks using full-batch gradient flow and DMFT in sparse linear regression, rather than the architectures, discrete training recipes, and measurements in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization scale α changes fixed-point test error and convergence speed; regularization λ and aspect ratio δ distinguish the analyzed regimes.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller initialization improves fixed-point test error but slows convergence in unregularized, overparameterized sparse regression with diagonal linear networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale trades off generalization against convergence speed in diagonal linear networks trained by full-batch gradient flow on sparse regression.

fits_no_version.finding: At regularized fixed points, Etest/Etrain = (1 + χw)^2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Integrated susceptibility determines the test-to-training error ratio in the study's regularized diagonal linear regression analysis.

record.problems: The timescale analysis is described as heuristic and its rigorous treatment is stated to be beyond the paper's scope. The generalization result is derived for sparse regression, and the real-world convergence-rate results quantitatively deviate from theory, which the authors attribute most likely to a finite-sample effect.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results omitted. The paper's discussion of prior studies is cited background rather than results from this study.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width required for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and transferred initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning budgets, weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover held-out performance.
Dropout's effect on held-out error and its dependence on data size, strength, and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because no row measures a version. This does not dispute the reported initialization effects. Appendix C.2.1 derives a noisy-regression interpolation peak as δ approaches 1 from above, but varies the sample-to-feature ratio rather than network width, so it does not test V2.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and optimizer tuning.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: diagonal linear networks (DLNs)
rows.size_stated: n, d → ∞ with n/d → δ ∈ (0, ∞); simulations use d = 500
rows.operation_detail: Varied initialization scale α and measured fixed-point test error in the unregularized overparameterized case.
rows.value: Smaller initialization α leads to better generalization; numerical values are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 2a simulations run 10 times on independent data; error bars indicate one standard deviation.
rows.note: The text states the direction of the effect; the plotted numerical values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The initialization effect is reported correctly but measures no claim version. Separate Gaussian simulations (d = 500) from gene-expression-feature simulations (n = 100, d = 200). Both use sparse regression targets; this is not natural-label image classification.

rows.subject: diagonal linear networks (DLNs)
rows.size_stated: n, d → ∞ with n/d → δ ∈ (0, ∞); simulations use d = 500
rows.stage_stated: full-batch gradient flow; convergence to fixed point
rows.operation_detail: Varied initialization scale α and measured the loss convergence rate in the unregularized case.

conditions.value: δ < 1 for Figure 2; δ = 2 and δ = 0.5 for Figure 13

rows.measure: exponential convergence rate γ of the loss
rows.value: The exponent γ is monotonically increasing with respect to α; smaller initialization leads to slower convergence. Numerical curves are figure only.
rows.note: The monotonicity and direction are stated in the text; numerical rates are shown in figures.
rows.check: Convergence speed measures no claim version. The theoretical positivity and monotonicity statement in Proposition C.1 excludes δ = 1. Figure 2c also reports real-feature simulations with d = 200, whose rates agree qualitatively but deviate quantitatively from theory.

rows.subject: diagonal linear networks (DLNs)
rows.size_stated: high-dimensional limit; n, d → ∞ with n/d → δ ∈ (0, ∞)
rows.operation_detail: Related the fixed-point susceptibility χw to the ratio of training and test errors.
rows.measure: ratio between fixed-point training and test errors
rows.value: (1 + χw)^2 equals the ratio between fixed points of training and test errors, Etrain = Cf and Etest = Cw + σ².
rows.note: This is an explicit relationship between a measured property and the train/test error gap; it is not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
rows.check: Specify the ratio's direction: Equation C.12 gives Etest/Etrain = (1 + χw)^2, not Etrain/Etest. Susceptibility is an integrated response, not V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
